alertDetailsOverride.alertDisplayNameFormat: Azure management access from new IP {{IPAddress}} by {{UserPrincipalName}}
alertDetailsOverride.alertDescriptionFormat: {{UserPrincipalName}} accessed {{AppDisplayName}} from {{IPAddress}}, an address not seen for Azure management access in the previous 14 days.

properties.query:
let MgmtApps = dynamic(["Azure Portal", "Windows Azure Service Management API", "Microsoft Azure CLI", "Microsoft Azure PowerShell", "Azure Resource Manager"]);
let Baseline = SigninLogs
    | where TimeGenerated between (ago(14d) .. ago(1d))
    | where ResultType == "0"
    | where AppDisplayName has_any (MgmtApps);
let KnownIps = Baseline | distinct IPAddress;
let KnownClients = Baseline
    | where isnotempty(UserAgent)
    | extend UAFamily = replace_regex(tolower(UserAgent), @"[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)+", "")
    | distinct UAFamily;
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where ResultType == "0"
| where AppDisplayName has_any (MgmtApps)
| where IPAddress !in (KnownIps)
| extend UAFamily = replace_regex(tolower(UserAgent), @"[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)+", "")
| where isempty(UserAgent) or UAFamily !in (KnownClients)
| project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, IPAddress, UserAgent, AppDisplayName, Location, ResultType
| extend Account = UserPrincipalName, IP = IPAddress
properties.displayName: Identity - Azure Management Plane Access from New IP
properties.description:
DETECTS
Successful authentication to Azure Portal, ARM, Azure CLI, or Azure PowerShell from an IP not previously used for management access in 14 days.

WHY IT MATTERS
Deliberately narrower than general sign-in anomaly detection. Access to the management plane is what allows an attacker to alter infrastructure, escalate via RBAC, and disable logging. Scoping the anomaly to management applications only raises severity while cutting noise, since these apps have a much smaller and more stable legitimate IP set than mail or Teams.

TRIAGE
1. Confirm the user routinely performs Azure administration.
2. Geolocate the IP and check whether it belongs to a hosting or VPN provider, which is unusual for admin access.
3. Immediately review AzureActivity for that Caller in the same window. This rule pairs directly with the control-plane rules.
4. Verify with the user out of band.
5. If unexplained: revoke sessions and audit every control-plane action taken from that session.

FALSE POSITIVES
Admins working from a new location, a changed VPN egress, or a newly provisioned jump host. Expect noise in the first 14 days while the baseline builds.

SOURCE
SigninLogs

TUNING HISTORY (2026-08-02)
Now requires BOTH a new IP and a new client, rather than IP alone. The operator connects
through a mobile VPN whose exit nodes rotate every session - 15 distinct source IPs were
observed in a 38-hour window - so IP novelty on its own fired on every legitimate sign-in
and could never indicate an intruder. UserAgent is stable across that rotation: one UA
spanned 13 distinct IPs, another 11, which makes the client the usable fingerprint and the
IP the noisy dimension. UserAgent is normalised by stripping version numbers, because a
Chrome 150 to 151 upgrade occurred inside the baseline window and a full-string match would
treat every browser update as a new client.
CAVEAT: UserAgent is client-supplied and therefore attacker-controllable. This is a noise
reducer, not an authenticator. An adversary replaying a stolen token with a copied UA will
not trigger this rule, and Chrome-on-Windows is among the most common UA strings in
existence. For a control that survives deliberate spoofing, correlate on ASN or impossible
travel instead. Validated against live data at deployment: zero rows, confirming legitimate
VPN rotation is suppressed.
